item.title: This NOV. 5: two Hudson friends who shaped and documented defini...
item.description: This NOV. 5: two Hudson friends who shaped and documented defining eras of rock'n'roll lead a conversation about music, memory, and creative community!Former bassist of seminal ‘9s rock bands Hole and The Smashing Pumpkins and Basilica Hudson co-founder Melissa Auf der Maur joins artist and director Michael Lindsay-Hogg to discuss two extraordinary chapters of music history, followed by a Q&A, book signing, and reception with music by DJBNNYBRNS.Celebrating her 6 memoir, Even the Good Girls Will Cry, and companion photo book, My ’9s Rock Photographs, Auf der Maur shares stories from alternative rock’s ‘9s heyday alongside Lindsay-Hogg, whose work with The Beatles and The Rolling Stones includes Let It Be and The Rolling Stones Rock and Roll Circus. ️ Tickets Available Now + Books for SaleThursday, Nov. 5, 6 | 6: PM

item.title: LEGENDARY ️! Melissa Auf der Maur In Conversation w/ @carmelho...
item.description: LEGENDARY ️! Melissa Auf der Maur In Conversation w/ @carmelholt ️Author and musician @xmadmx (Hole, Smashing Pumpkins, solo) in conversation with Carmel Holt (host of SHEROES Radio + Podcast) about her life, career, and NEW book, “Even the Good Girls Will Cry: A ’9s Rock Memoir.” ️Sunday, October 11⌚️ : pm - 3: pm ️ Old Dutch Church, 7 Wall St. Kingston, NY ‍ Before becoming the bassist for ‘9s alternative rock bands Hole and, later, the Smashing Pumpkins, Montreal-born Melissa Auf der Maur studied photography at Concordia niversity. She maintained her daily practice while on the road, requesting a roll of 35mm film at every venue as part of her rider and resulting in over 1, images documenting life onstage and away from the crowds. A major exhibition of Auf der Maur’s photographs is on view at the Art Gallery of Ontario from September , 6, and is accompanied by a hardback photobook that includes over of the musician’s photographs, published by the AGO and DelMonico Books. Auf der Maur’s photographs have been featured in publications including National Geographic and Spin, among others. In 1 she co founded the nonprofit arts and performance center Basilica Hudson, located in upstate New York. This past March, Auf der Maur published her memoir, Even the Good Girls Will Cry. *photo by Norman Jean RoyBONS !! Copies of “Even the Good Girls Will Cry: A ’9s Rock Memoir” will be available for sale at this event! Come out and support one of the GREATS ️ Full O+ Festival schedule + by-donation wristbands are available NOW @ the link in our bio, or: opositivefestival.org!

item.title: A substantial feature on Melissa Auf der Maur: My ’9s Rock Pho...
item.description: A substantial feature on Melissa Auf der Maur: My ’9s Rock Photographs by @ivadixit in the current issue of @aperturefnd・・・While playing bass for Hole in the 199s, Melissa Auf der Maur created a searing record of life on tour in an offline world.Auf der Maur (@xmadmx) became a relentless documentarian of her life, relying on a 8mm point-and-shoot Nikon and the occasional one-hour photo lab whenever she could find one in between tour stops. During that period, she took nearly ten thousand photographs, most of which have languished in her attic in upstate New York—until now. This month, the exhibition “Melissa Auf der Maur: My ’9s Rock Photographs” opened at @agotoronto, where two hundred photographs from her personal archive will be on display.In tour buses, hotel rooms, dressing rooms, sets, stadiums, and arenas—where thousands of people convulsed around her electric presence onstage—Auf der Maur photographed her life as a musician and the people in it with a raw spontaneity and irreverence. “So much 199s nostalgia overlooks the anger and restlessness of those growing up in an era of seismic change,” writes Iva Dixit.See Aperture’s link in bio to read more about Melissa Auf der Maur’s ’9s grunge diary, now online from Aperture’s latest issue “Stop Time.”All photographs by Melissa Auf der Maur. Images (in order): Self-Portrait in Yellow Light from Celebrity Skin cover shoot, 1998; Self-portrait with Hole, Lollapalooza, 1995; Burning Billboard from “Malibu” music video set, 1998; Self-portrait on Stage with the Smashing Pumpkins, Cape Town, South Africa, ; Courtney on Tarmac, 1999On view at @agotorontoCatalog co-published by @delmonico_books

item.title: MSEM x BOOK NVEILEDPHOTOGRAPHY: My first love, BT as most of you...
item.description: MSEM x BOOK NVEILEDPHOTOGRAPHY: My first love, BT as most of you know, i was hijacked by a rock band and took a LONG WILD detour, for a couple decades on the road, devoted to the POWER OF MSIC. Now a quarter century later, its time to purge, reflect and share.MY 9s Rock photographs exhibit and book, were unveiled this month, and pull from my archive of over 1, photographic negatives. This multimedia memoir project, is part of our collective memory, of what would become our last analog decade. This project is a form of collective mourning of what was lost, but also an opportunity to reclaim and explore a longing for the old / timeless ways we lived, and decide what we want to get back. Thx to @agotoronto @delmonico_books @artbook who have offered the DREAM PLATFORM to REFLECT and SHARE my human experience. Sharing is Caring ….Exhibit is up in Toronto until June 7.Book is available now online and in local bookstores near you.Soundtrack to the exhibit, BASS WOMB ROOM: My ‘9s 4-Track Demos x Field Recordings, is yours for streaming, and on cassette (and vinyl coming soon!). Central mission statement to the share and the care, is EVEN THE GOOD GIRLS WILL CRY: My ‘9s Rock Memoir — available at book shops, libraries and audiobook.Special thanks to my co-curators Sophie Hackett @hackettse Jim Shedden @jimshedden and archivist Katherine Driscoll @kathydisco and exhibition manager Chloe Wittes @chloeee491 for elevating my PRO-ANALOG HMAN Advocacy mission this year. Thank you Emilie Hanskamp @emilie.theaux for the museum launch conversation, and to Kelefa Sanneh for the meaningful @newyorkermag piece and conversation @strandbookstore for my NYC book launch - and the 1+ Toronto art lovers who came to the opening, and 4 New Yorkers who squeezed into the top floor of a book store for this.nveiled. Launched. Taking it on the road. Keep eyes peeled for book talks near you …Nowhere better than in a MSEM and BOOK (or a live music show!) to honor REAL LIFE in PERSON, in HAND exchange, connection and inspiration. Vive L’Art et Merci!xMxthx @laceysd @mike.nourse and @flexrflex for extra video / photos

item.title: In the summer of 1994, Montreal-born and -raised musician, artis...
item.description: In the summer of 1994, Montreal-born and -raised musician, artist, and author Melissa Auf der Maur (@xmadmx) catapulted to the red-hot center of ’9s alt-rock history when she became the bassist in @courtneylove’s band, Hole (@holemusic). Later, she would also join the @smashingpumpkins at the personal invitation of founder @billycorgan. Equipped with her trusty palm-size Nikon camera during those seismic, possibility-filled days, her pictures are now a rare visual time capsule of an era where analog ruled. Her new book, “My ’9s Rock Photographs” (DelMonico/D.A.P.)—co-published and accompanied by an exhibition at Toronto’s Art Gallery of Ontario (@agotoronto), on through June 6, 7—compiles her collection of more than once-in-a-generation photographs.In our newsletter’s latest “Interview With,” Auf der Maur speaks with senior editor Olivia Aylmer (@livlindsa) about the life-changing magic of the darkroom, recentering our humanity beyond the digital avalanche and the beauty in never being too cool to care.(Slide 1: Photo: @normanjeanroy; Slides 3, 5, 7, and 9: Photos: @xmadmx/Courtesy @delmonico_books and @artbook)
